screening_decisions.reason: Randomised double-blind trial of aminophylline (a theophylline analogue) versus placebo in patients with acute ischaemic stroke; treatment administered during acute hospitalization (within the acute window). Meets all criteria.

Randomised double-blind trial of intravenous aminophylline versus placebo in 79 patients with acute cerebral infarction; immediate injection in the acute phase implies initiation within one week. Meets all criteria.
Open-label, single-arm dose-escalation (no randomized control group). Does not meet the randomized, placebo/control comparison criterion.

Mixed-subject study of cerebral metabolism (vincamine and aminophylline) without clear randomisation or acute ischaemic stroke population or initiation within one week. Fails population/design/timing criteria.

Randomised cross-over physiologic study in patients recovering from an acute ischaemic stroke; intervention not initiated within one week of stroke onset and not an acute therapeutic RCT versus placebo/control for clinical outcomes.

Randomised cross-over physiologic study measuring cerebral blood flow in patients recovering from stroke; intervention occurs beyond the acute window (>1 week) and is not an acute treatment RCT versus placebo/control.
Non-randomised physiologic study of intracarotid aminophylline effects on cerebral blood flow; not a randomized placebo/control trial in acute ischaemic stroke.
Animal study in cats; not a human randomized trial in acute ischaemic stroke.
Animal study in dogs; not a human randomized trial in acute ischaemic stroke.
Narrative/mechanistic report on aminophylline; lacks randomized trial design in acute ischaemic stroke within one week of onset.
